a walk
a hit-by-pitch
being hit by a pitch
hitting the ball far without reaching base
solution: 안타, 볼넷, 몸에 맞는 공은 모두 선수가 안전하게 출루하는 방법이다. 공을 멀리 쳤더라도 출루하지 못했다면 안전하게 출루한 경우가 아니므로 ⑤가 적절하지 않다.

The ISS has been continuously occupied by astronauts for many years. Each of its many sections have a particular role, and together they make the station to serve as a research laboratory. Keeping every system work in orbit are one of the most difficult tasks human beings have undertaken.
answer: The ISS has been continuously occupied by astronauts for many years. Each of its many sections has a particular role, and together they make the station serve as a research laboratory. Keeping every system working in orbit is one of the most difficult tasks human beings have undertaken.
solution: 「each of＋복수 명사」의 주어는 단수로 취급하므로 have를 has로 고친다. make 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 to serve는 serve가 된다. keep은 「keep＋목적어＋현재분사」로 쓰며, 동명사구 Keeping every system working in orbit가 주어이므로 동사는 단수형 is가 알맞다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 질문에 대한 답의 빈칸에 들어갈 연속된 두 단어를 글에서 찾아 쓰시오.

People may expect to earn money by investing in stocks. However, investors also need to be ready to lose money.

Q. What must investors be prepared for besides earning money?
A. They must be prepared to ____________________.
solution: 글은 주식 투자로 돈을 벌 것이라는 기대와 돈을 잃을 가능성을 함께 제시한다. be ready to와 be prepared to는 모두 ‘~할 준비가 되어 있다’라는 뜻이므로 lose money가 들어간다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 질문에 대한 답의 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 글에서 찾아 쓰시오.

Investing offers a way to build wealth. Nevertheless, anyone entering the stock market should act with knowledge and caution.

Q. What should guide investors along with knowledge?
A. They should act with ____________________.
solution: 글은 투자자가 지식과 신중함을 갖추고 행동해야 한다고 설명한다. 질문의 along with knowledge는 본문의 knowledge and caution에서 knowledge와 짝을 이루는 말을 묻는다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 질문에 대한 답의 빈칸에 들어갈 연속된 네 단어를 글에서 찾아 쓰시오.

The stock market keeps changing. Because of these constant changes, investors face the possibility of loss and debt, even when they hope to earn money.

Q. What financial risks do investors face despite their hope of earning money?
A. They face the possibility ____________________.
solution: 질문의 financial risks는 글에서 주식 시장의 지속적인 변화로 발생할 수 있다고 설명한 손실과 부채를 가리킨다. 답안에 possibility가 이미 주어져 있으므로 그 뒤의 of loss and debt만 쓴다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 질문에 대한 답을 완성하시오. 각 빈칸에는 글에서 연속된 세 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

An interest in a company's products may help you choose an investment. Before investing, however, research the company and keep yourself informed. You should also consider your risk tolerance instead of focusing only on a possible profit.

Q. What should you do before investing, in addition to researching a company?
A. You should (가)____________________ and consider (나)____________________.

답은 (가), (나)의 순서로 쓰시오.
answer: keep yourself informed / your risk tolerance
solution: 질문의 in addition to researching a company는 회사 조사 이외의 행동을 찾으라는 뜻이다. 정보를 계속 파악하라는 keep yourself informed와 자신의 위험 감수 정도를 고려하라는 consider your risk tolerance가 해당한다.

body:
다음 문장에서 밑줄 친 enhances와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

Stretchable and breathable materials enhance the comfort of universal design clothing.
choices: reduce
improve
measure
limit
replace
solution: enhance는 ‘향상하다, 높이다’라는 뜻이다. 문맥상 신축성과 통기성이 좋은 소재가 옷의 편안함을 높인다는 의미이므로 improve가 가장 적절하다.

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

In universal design clothing, magnets and Velcro can be used in place of ______.
choices: sleeves
waistbands
buttons
materials
barriers
solution: 유니버설 디자인 의류에서는 옷을 쉽게 입고 벗을 수 있도록 단추 대신 자석과 벨크로를 사용한다. 따라서 buttons가 알맞다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
choices: Magnets makes clothing easier to wear.
Stretchable materials improves mobility.
Adjustable sleeves allows wearers to move freely.
Universal design clothing benefits people of different abilities.
Inclusive word choices reduces potential barriers.
solution: ④의 주어 Universal design clothing은 단수이고 동사 benefits가 이에 알맞게 쓰였다. 나머지는 모두 복수 주어에 단수 동사 makes, improves, allows, reduces를 사용한 수 일치 오류가 있다.

body:
다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Inclusive communication involves selecting words that (A) avoid / avoids prejudice. It encourages participation, (B) invite / inviting more people into society. In addition, expressions related to medical conditions should (C) consider / be considered carefully.
choices: avoid ― inviting ― be considered
avoid ― invite ― consider
avoids ― inviting ― be considered
avoids ― invite ― consider
avoid ― inviting ― consider
solution: (A)의 선행사 words가 복수이므로 avoid가 알맞다. (B)는 앞 절의 결과를 덧붙이는 분사구문이므로 inviting을 쓰고, (C)는 표현이 신중하게 고려되는 것이므로 수동태 be considered가 필요하다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 주어진 말을 모두 활용하여 문장을 완성하시오.

포용적 언어를 사용하는 것은 모든 사람이 사회에 참여하도록 장려한다.

(invites / inclusive language / participate / using / everyone / society / to / in)
answer: Using inclusive language invites everyone to participate in society.
solution: 동명사구 Using inclusive language가 문장의 주어이므로 단수 동사 invites를 사용한다. invite의 목적어 everyone 뒤에는 목적격 보어 역할을 하는 to participate가 이어진다.

body:
다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Replacing expressions that carry racial or gender bias with (A) terms can lower barriers and strengthen people's sense of (B).
choices: conventional ― mobility
neutral ― belonging
adjustable ― equality
medical ― convenience
breathable ― participation
solution: 편견을 담은 표현은 중립적인 표현으로 바꾸어야 하므로 (A)에는 neutral이 알맞다. 이러한 언어 사용은 사람들의 소속감을 높이므로 (B)에는 belonging이 들어간다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

Universal design clothing ①uses stretchable materials to improve comfort. Magnets and Velcro ②make the clothing easier to handle, and adjustable sleeves allow people ③to dress independently. These features are useful not only for people with disabilities but also for those ④experiencing temporary injuries. As a result, wearers of different abilities can ⑤enjoys greater convenience and mobility.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
solution: 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 enjoys를 enjoy로 고쳐야 한다. ④의 experiencing은 those를 뒤에서 수식하는 현재분사로 적절하다.

body:
다음 두 문장의 의미가 같도록 빈칸을 완성하시오.

Universal design clothing replaces buttons with magnets and Velcro. Therefore, wearers can put it on and take it off more easily.

By replacing buttons with magnets and Velcro, universal design clothing ________________________________.
answer: makes it easier for wearers to put it on and take it off
solution: ‘make it＋형용사＋for 목적어＋to부정사’는 ‘목적어가 ~하는 것을 …하게 만들다’라는 뜻이다. 비교급 의미를 유지하기 위해 easier를 사용하고, 입고 벗는다는 의미는 put it on and take it off로 나타낸다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 (A)~(C)에 각각 한 단어를 쓰시오.

포용적 언어를 사용함으로써 우리는 편견을 줄일 뿐만 아니라 모두가 소속감을 느끼는 더욱 환영받는 환경을 만들 수 있다.

By using inclusive language, we can not only (A) ______ bias but also (B) ______ a more welcoming environment where everyone feels a sense of (C) ______.
solution: not only A but also B에는 문법적으로 대등한 표현이 와야 하므로 조동사 can 뒤에 동사원형 reduce와 create를 쓴다. ‘소속감’은 a sense of belonging으로 표현하므로 (C)에는 belonging이 알맞다.

body:
다음 문장에서 어법상 잘못된 네 단어를 찾아 문맥에 맞게 고친 형태를 순서대로 쓰시오.

Choosing neutral alternatives help reduce barriers, made communication more thoughtful. Expressions associated with prejudice should replaced when they causes some people to feel excluded.
solution: 동명사구 Choosing neutral alternatives가 단수 주어이므로 help를 helps로 고친다. 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문에는 making이 필요하고, 조동사 should 뒤의 수동태는 be replaced로 쓴다. 마지막으로 주어 they가 복수이므로 causes를 cause로 고친다.

body:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 부분을 어법에 맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

Anyone who invests in stocks must be prepared ⓐ losing money because the market can fluctuate.
solution: ‘~할 준비가 되어 있다’는 「be prepared to＋동사원형」으로 표현한다. 따라서 동명사 losing을 to lose로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 부분을 어법에 맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

An official market ⓐ calling a stock exchange allows investors to buy and sell stocks.
solution: market은 ‘증권 거래소라고 불리는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미가 필요하다. 따라서 현재분사 calling을 과거분사 called로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 부분을 어법에 맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

When economic conditions are favorable, investors may ⓐ increases their stock purchases.
solution: 조동사 may 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 한다. 따라서 increases를 increase로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓒ 중 어법상 어색한 것 하나를 골라 기호를 쓰고, 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

Before investing, do your research, ⓐ staying informed about the company, and ⓑ be mindful of the risk you may ⓒ face.
solution: do, stay, be는 투자자가 해야 할 일을 나열하는 병렬 구조이다. 따라서 do 및 be와 형태를 맞추어 staying을 동사원형 stay로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓒ 중 어법상 어색한 것 하나를 골라 기호를 쓰고, 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

In a rising market, stock purchases often ⓐ increase, and investors ⓑ maintaining their investments because they ⓒ feel confident.
solution: and 뒤 절에는 주어 investors에 이어지는 서술 동사가 필요하다. 문맥상 현재의 일반적인 상황을 나타내므로 maintaining을 maintain으로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓒ 중 어법상 어색한 것 하나를 골라 기호를 쓰고, 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

A bear market ⓐ is occurred when economic conditions are unfavorable and stock values ⓑ decline, which may cause investors ⓒ to sell their stocks.
solution: occur는 ‘발생하다’라는 뜻의 자동사이므로 수동태로 쓸 수 없다. 따라서 is occurred를 능동형 occurs로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 골라 기호를 쓰고, 각각 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

ⓐ Thinking of a bull raising its horns when you picture a rising market. Investors in such a market often ⓑ feel confident, ⓒ buy more stocks, and ⓓ maintaining their investments as stock values ⓔ rise.
solution: 첫 문장은 독자에게 지시하는 명령문이므로 Thinking을 동사원형 Think로 고쳐야 한다. 또한 feel, buy, maintain이 often에 이어 병렬로 연결되므로 maintaining은 maintain이 되어야 한다.

body:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 골라 기호를 쓰고, 각각 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

The stock market constantly fluctuates, ⓐ created a risk of loss for investors. Anyone ⓑ investing in stocks should ⓒ research the companies, ⓓ stays informed about them, and ⓔ be mindful of personal risk tolerance.
solution: 시장의 변동이 위험을 만들어 내는 부수적 결과를 나타내므로 created는 분사구문인 creating으로 고쳐야 한다. 조동사 should 뒤에서 research, stay, be가 병렬로 연결되므로 stays는 stay가 되어야 한다.

body:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 골라 기호를 쓰고, 각각 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

Stocks can ⓐ be bought through an official market where people can easily ⓑ buying or ⓒ sell them. Share this information with friends ⓓ whom may be interested in learning more about economics and ⓔ investing.
solution: 조동사 can 뒤에서는 buy와 sell이 동사원형으로 병렬을 이루어야 하므로 buying을 buy로 고쳐야 한다. 관계대명사는 뒤 절에서 주어 역할을 하므로 목적격 whom이 아니라 주격 who가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 네 개 골라 기호를 쓰고, 각각 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

Stock-market movement ⓐ can divide into rising and falling trends. High employment rates and GDP increases ⓑ are positive economic indicators associated with favorable conditions. In a rising market, investors often respond by increasing their stock purchases and ⓒ maintain their investments. By contrast, a bear market ⓓ is occurred when conditions are unfavorable and stock values decline. Before choosing an investment, make sure to ⓔ doing research, stay informed about the company, and be mindful of the risk. This advice can also be shared with friends ⓕ who are interested in economics.
answer: ⓐ can divide → can be divided, ⓒ maintain → maintaining, ⓓ is occurred → occurs, ⓔ doing → do
solution: 시장의 움직임은 두 추세로 ‘나뉘는’ 대상이므로 can be divided가 적절하다. 전치사 by 뒤에서는 increasing과 maintaining이 병렬을 이루어야 하며, 자동사 occur는 수동태가 아니라 occurs로 써야 한다. 또한 「make sure to＋동사원형」의 구조에 따라 doing은 do로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성할 때 가장 적절한 것은?

The flight control team arranges each astronaut’s schedule. The crew members follow the plan while conducting scientific experiments and taking care of the space station.

<보기> A, Careful, Plan, Day, In, Space
choices: A Careful Day Planning in Space
A Carefully Planned Day in Space
A Day Carefully Planning Space
In Space a Day Carefully Plans
A Planned Space in a Careful Day
solution: 우주에서의 하루가 지상 관제팀에 의해 세심하게 계획된다는 내용이다. Careful은 부사 Carefully로, Plan은 수동의 의미를 나타내는 Planned로 바꾸어야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성할 때 가장 적절한 것은?

Back on the ground, the astronaut can once more smell grass and feel the wind and rain. These ordinary experiences now seem wonderful and unforgettable.

<보기> The, Magic, Of, Be, Home, Again
choices: Being the Magic of Home Again
Again Being Home of the Magic
The Magic of Being Home Again
The Home of Magic Being Again
Being Again the Home of Magic
solution: 귀환 후 다시 집에 있다는 사실에서 느끼는 경이로움이 글의 중심이다. 전치사 of 뒤에서 Be는 동명사 Being으로 바뀌어야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성할 때 가장 적절한 것은?

The crew sees the sun rise and set repeatedly as the station circles the planet. Nevertheless, their schedule follows Greenwich Mean Time.

<보기> Live, By, Earth, Time, In, Orbit
choices: Living by Earth Time in Orbit
Earth Living by Orbit in Time
Time in Earth by Living Orbit
Living in Earth Time by Orbit
Orbiting by Live Time in Earth
solution: 우주정거장의 반복되는 일출과 일몰에도 우주인들은 지구의 시간을 따른다. Live를 Living으로 바꾼 「Living by Earth Time in Orbit」가 글을 가장 정확히 요약한다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성할 때 가장 적절한 것은?

Immediately after the capsule reaches the ground, the astronaut’s arms and legs seem unusually heavy. Readjusting to gravity cannot be completed in a short time.

<보기> Why, Thing, Feel, Heavy, After, Land
choices: Why Landing Feels Heavy After Things
Why Things Felt Heavily After Land
Why Heavy Things Feel After Landing
Why Things Feel Heavy After Landing
Why Landing Things Feel After Heavy
solution: 착륙 후 중력 때문에 여러 신체 부위와 물건이 무겁게 느껴지는 이유를 다룬 글이다. Thing은 복수형 Things로, Land는 전치사 after의 목적어인 Landing으로 바꾸는 것이 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성할 때 가장 적절한 것은?

One experiment especially pleases the astronaut: raising basil from seeds and recording its growth. The green plant brings joy to life aboard the station.

<보기> Grow, Basil, A, Green, Delight, In, Space
choices: Basil Growing in a Delight Green Space
A Green Space Growing in Basil Delight
Growing Basil: A Green Delight in Space
A Delight Growing Green Space in Basil
In Green Space: A Basil Growing Delight
solution: 우주에서 바질을 기르는 실험과 초록 식물이 주는 기쁨이 핵심이다. Grow를 동명사 Growing으로 바꾼 「Growing Basil: A Green Delight in Space」가 자연스럽다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성할 때 가장 적절한 것은? (필요시 변형할 것)

Before beginning work, the astronaut checks the schedule sent by the flight control team and later meets with that team. Every part of the working day has already been arranged by people on the ground.

<보기> How, an Astronaut’s, Workday, Be, Plan, On, Earth
choices: How Earth Is Planned on an Astronaut’s Workday
How an Astronaut’s Workday Is Planned on Earth
How an Astronaut’s Planned Workday Is on Earth
How on Earth an Astronaut’s Workday Plans
How an Astronaut’s Workday Plans to Be on Earth
solution: 우주인의 근무 일정이 지구에서 계획된다는 내용이다. Workday가 계획을 받는 대상이므로 Be와 Plan을 Is Planned라는 수동태로 변형해야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (필요시 변형할 것)

The capsule enters the resistant atmosphere and becomes extremely hot. Flames pass its darkened window before a parachute slows the capsule and carries the crew closer to the ground.

<보기> A, Fiery, Descend, Through, The, Atmosphere, Toward, Home

A ________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________
answer: A Fiery Descent Through the Atmosphere Toward Home
solution: 고온과 불꽃을 견디며 대기권을 통과하여 귀환하는 과정이 중심이다. Descend는 관사와 형용사의 수식을 받는 명사 Descent로 바꾸어야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성할 때 가장 적절한 것은? (필요시 변형할 것)

While still inside the sleeping bag, the astronaut brushes their teeth. Since floating toothpaste cannot easily be spat out, it is swallowed with water from a bag.

<보기> Why, Astronaut, Swallow, Toothpaste, In, Space
choices: Why Astronauts Swallow Toothpaste in Space
Why Space Swallows an Astronaut’s Toothpaste
Why an Astronaut Is Swallowed in Space Toothpaste
Why Toothpaste Swallows Astronauts in Space
Why Astronauts in Toothpaste Swallow Space
solution: 무중력 상태에서는 치약을 뱉기 어려워 삼킨다는 내용이다. 일반적인 우주인들을 나타내도록 Astronaut를 Astronauts로 바꾼 ①이 의미와 어법에 모두 맞는다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (필요시 변형할 것)

The ground team decides the details of the crew’s schedule. On the station, an astronaut follows that plan while performing experiments and maintenance throughout the working day.

<보기> An, ISS, Day, Plan, On, Earth, And, Spend, Work

________ ________ ________: ________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________
answer: An ISS Day: Planned on Earth and Spent Working
solution: 우주정거장의 하루는 지구에서 계획되고 우주인의 업무 수행으로 채워진다. Plan과 Spend는 수동의 과거분사 Planned와 Spent로, Work는 Spent의 보어 역할을 하는 Working으로 변형해야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 제목을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (필요시 변형할 것)

During the return, the crew endures intense heat as the capsule passes through the atmosphere. After landing, the smell of grass and the touch of wind and rain reveal the wonder of familiar life on the planet.

<보기> Survive, The, Heat, To, Rediscover, Earth, Everyday, Magic

________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________
answer: Surviving the Heat to Rediscover Earth’s Everyday Magic
solution: 대기권 재진입의 열기를 견딘 뒤 지구의 평범한 것들이 지닌 경이로움을 새롭게 깨닫는 내용이다. Survive는 주제를 나타내는 동명사 Surviving으로, Earth는 소유격 Earth’s로 변형해야 한다.

body:
다음 우리말과 의미가 같도록 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 문장을 완성하시오.

데이터 팀은 선수들을 영입하기 위해 많은 양의 데이터를 분석했다.

<보기> analyze / the data team / players / large amounts of data / recruit
<조건> 과거시제와 목적을 나타내는 to부정사를 사용할 것
answer: The data team analyzed large amounts of data to recruit players.
solution: ‘많은 양의 데이터’는 large amounts of data로 표현한다. 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 to recruit players를 문장 끝에 배치하고, analyze는 과거형 analyzed로 쓴다.

body:
다음 우리말과 의미가 같도록 주어진 단어를 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

공의 솔기는 투수들이 공의 방향과 속도를 조절하도록 돕는다.

<보기> its / help / direction / the ball’s seams / pitchers / and / control / speed
<조건> help+목적어+동사원형의 구조를 사용할 것
answer: The ball’s seams help pitchers control its direction and speed.
solution: help 뒤에는 목적어 pitchers와 동사원형 control이 차례로 온다. its direction and speed는 투수들이 조절하는 대상을 나타낸다.

body:
다음 우리말과 의미가 같도록 <보기>의 단어를 활용하여 문장을 완성하시오. 필요하면 형태를 바꿀 수 있다.

그 데이터는 경기 중에 전술적 결정을 내리는 데 사용되었다.

<보기> data / use / make / tactical decisions / during games
<조건> 수동태와 to부정사를 사용할 것
answer: The data was used to make tactical decisions during games.
solution: ‘사용되었다’는 과거 수동태 was used로 표현한다. 데이터의 사용 목적은 to make tactical decisions로 나타낸다.

body:
다음 우리말과 의미가 같도록 주어진 표현을 모두 사용하여 문장을 완성하시오.

그 구단이 2020년에 리그 우승을 하기 전에 데이터 팀은 주요 분야에 데이터 분석을 적용했었다.

<보기> apply data analysis / the data team / win the league championship / key areas / before / in 2020
<조건> 먼저 일어난 일을 과거완료로 나타낼 것
answer: The data team had applied data analysis to key areas before the club won the league championship in 2020.
solution: 우승보다 데이터 분석의 적용이 먼저 일어났으므로 had applied의 과거완료를 사용한다. before절의 우승은 단순과거 won으로 나타낸다.

body:
다음 우리말과 의미가 같도록 문장을 완성하시오.

새로운 데이터 팀은 데이터에 상당한 전문 지식을 지닌 사람들로 구성되었다.

<조건> consist of와 주격 관계대명사 who를 사용할 것
<보기> people / significant expertise / the new data team / data / have
answer: The new data team consisted of people who had significant expertise in data.
solution: ‘~로 구성되었다’는 consisted of로 표현한다. people을 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사 who 뒤에 had significant expertise in data를 연결한다.

body:
다음 우리말과 의미가 같도록 <보기>의 표현을 모두 사용하여 문장을 완성하시오. 필요하면 형태를 바꿀 수 있다.

새 구단주는 구단이 데이터 분석을 새로운 수준으로 끌어올리기 위해 새로운 데이터 팀을 구성할 것을 요구했다.

<보기> the new owner / demand / the club / form / a new data team / push / data analysis / new heights
<조건> demand 뒤에 that절을 쓰고, that절의 동사는 원형으로 쓸 것
answer: The new owner demanded that the club form a new data team to push data analysis to new heights.
solution: 요구를 나타내는 demanded 뒤의 that절에서는 동사원형 form을 사용한다. 새로운 팀을 구성하는 목적은 to push data analysis to new heights로 표현한다.

body:
다음 우리말과 의미가 같도록 <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 22단어로 영작하시오. 필요하면 형태를 바꿀 수 있다.

그 팀은 선수들이 안정적인 심박수를 유지하도록 돕기 위해 얼굴색 변화가 심박수로 변환되는 시스템을 개발했다.

<보기> stable / develop / facial color variations / players / a system / convert / the team / heart rates / help / in which / into / maintain
<조건> 관계사, 수동태, 목적을 나타내는 to부정사를 각각 사용할 것
answer: The team developed a system in which facial color variations were converted into heart rates to help players maintain stable heart rates.
solution: a system 뒤에는 관계사 표현 in which를 사용하여 시스템 안에서 이루어지는 과정을 설명한다. ‘변환되는’은 수동태 were converted로 쓰고, 시스템의 목적은 to help로 나타낸다. help 뒤에는 목적어 players와 동사원형 maintain이 이어진다.

body:
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말을 어법에 맞게 연결한 것은?

Universal design aims to make everyday life easier for everyone. It is important (A)[to create / create] products that different people can use comfortably. Such products should be (B)[simple / simply] to use. People with different physical needs (C)[benefit / benefits] from this approach.
choices: to create — simply — benefit
create — simple — benefits
to create — simple — benefit
create — simply — benefit
to create — simple — benefits
solution: 가주어 It에 대응하는 진주어 자리이므로 (A)에는 to create가 알맞다. (B)는 be동사의 보어이므로 형용사 simple이 필요하다. (C)의 주어는 복수 명사 People이므로 benefit을 쓴다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 괄호 (A), (B), (C)의 표현을 어법에 맞게 고른 것은?

Some everyday tools (A)[design / are designed] mainly for right-handed users. Left-handed people may find these tools difficult to use. They sometimes look for products (B)[which / who] suit their needs. When suitable products are unavailable, they have no choice but (C)[to accept / accept] the inconvenience.
choices: design — which — to accept
are designed — who — accept
design — who — to accept
are designed — which — accept
are designed — which — to accept
solution: 도구는 설계되는 대상이므로 (A)에는 수동태 are designed가 필요하다. (B)는 사물인 products를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. (C)는 ‘~할 수밖에 없다’라는 have no choice but to부정사 구문이므로 to accept가 정답이다.

body:
괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 적절한 표현을 골라 바르게 연결한 것은?

Ronald Mace experienced difficulties with access to university facilities. While (A)[studying / studied] architecture, he encountered barriers caused by building designs. These difficulties encouraged him (B)[to seek / seeking] environments that everyone could use. His idea of universal design concerns all people, not just those (C)[who / which] have disabilities.
choices: studying — to seek — who
studied — to seek — who
studying — seeking — which
studied — seeking — who
studying — to seek — which
solution: While절에서 주절과 같은 주어 he와 be동사가 생략되었고, 그가 공부하는 주체이므로 (A)는 studying이다. encourage는 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 (B)는 to seek이다. (C)의 선행사 those는 사람들을 뜻하므로 who가 알맞다.

body:
다음 글의 논리와 문장 구조를 고려할 때, 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 표현으로 어법상 옳은 것은?

People may take it for granted (A)[that / what] everyday objects suit the needs of most users. Yet those whose needs differ from the majority's may experience discomfort. What universal design seeks to offer (B)[is / are] environments that people with different needs can share. Its aim is a community (C)[which / in which] no one is prevented by design barriers from using its facilities.
choices: what — is — in which
that — are — which
what — are — in which
that — is — in which
that — is — which
solution: (A)는 가목적어 it에 대응하는 진목적어절을 이끌며, 뒤에 완전한 절이 오므로 that이다. (B)는 보어 environments가 아니라 하나의 내용을 나타내는 주어절 What universal design seeks to offer에 일치시켜 is를 쓴다. (C)의 뒤에는 완전한 절이 이어지므로 장소의 의미를 더하는 in which가 필요하다.

body:
다음 글의 괄호 (A)~(E)에서 어법상 적절한 표현을 각각 고르시오. 답은 (A)부터 (E)까지 고른 표현만 순서대로 쉼표로 구분하여 쓰시오.

What people with different physical needs encounter in daily life (A)[is / are] often a series of barriers created by design. Some objects are suitable only for (B)[what / which] the majority regards as normal. People whose needs such objects fail to meet either put up with the difficulty or (C)[seek / seeking] alternatives. Those alternatives, some of (D)[which / them] are difficult to find, are designed for particular users. Universal design aims to make it possible for everyone's needs (E)[to consider / to be considered] from the beginning.
answer: is, what, seek, which, to be considered
solution: (A)는 일상에서 마주하는 내용을 하나로 나타내는 What절이 주어이므로 is이며, (B)는 전치사의 목적어절을 이끌면서 regards의 목적어 역할도 하는 what이다. (C)는 either A or B로 put up with와 병렬을 이루므로 seek가 알맞다. (D)는 두 절을 연결하는 관계대명사가 필요하므로 which이며, (E)는 needs가 고려되는 대상이므로 수동형 to be considered이다.

body:
괄호 (A)~(E) 중 어법에 맞는 표현을 각각 선택하시오. 선택한 표현만 (A)부터 (E)까지 순서대로 쉼표로 구분하여 쓰시오.

It was the difficulty Ronald Mace experienced at university (A)[that / what] helped shape his interest in design for everyone. While (B)[studying / studied] architecture, he found that some campus facilities were hard for him to access. The experience inspired him (C)[to imagine / imagining] a world in which products and environments would serve people with diverse needs. The environments he hoped to create were ones (D)[which / in which] could be used comfortably by everyone. What mattered in his approach was (E)[that / what] differences in age, size, or ability should not prevent people from using them.
answer: that, studying, to imagine, which, that
solution: (A)는 the difficulty Ronald Mace experienced at university를 강조하는 It was ~ that 강조 구문이므로 that이다. (B)는 주어 he가 공부하는 주체이므로 studying이고, (C)는 inspire의 목적격 보어이므로 to imagine이다. (D)는 뒤의 could be used의 주어가 필요하므로 which이며, (E)는 완전한 절을 보어로 이끄는 접속사 that이다.

body:
다음 글의 괄호 (A)~(E)에서 어법상 알맞은 표현을 고르시오. 정답은 고른 표현만 (A)부터 (E)까지 순서대로 쉼표로 구분하여 쓰시오.

The principles of universal design require products to be used simply and (A)[intuitive / intuitively]. They also call for enough space for users and for physical effort (B)[to minimize / to be minimized]. These principles make it clear (C)[that / what] accessibility involves more than the needs of a small group. A community in which facilities are convenient and pleasant to use (D)[benefits / benefit] from this approach. Nevertheless, what has been done to accommodate everyone (E)[has / have] not yet been enough.
answer: intuitively, to be minimized, that, benefits, has
solution: (A)는 simply와 병렬을 이루어 be used를 수식하므로 부사 intuitively이다. (B)는 physical effort가 최소화되는 대상이므로 수동형 to be minimized이며, (C)는 가목적어 it에 대응하는 완전한 진목적어절을 이끄는 that이다. (D)의 주어는 관계절 안의 facilities가 아니라 단수 명사 A community이므로 benefits이다. (E)는 지금까지 이루어진 일을 하나의 내용으로 나타내는 what절이 주어이므로 has를 쓴다.

body:
다음 글에서 설명하는 ISS의 용도로 알맞은 것은?

The International Space Station provides a place for scientific research in subjects such as physics and medicine. Astronauts also use it to test spacecraft systems that may be needed for future journeys to the moon, Mars, or asteroids. The station includes areas for experiments and areas where astronauts live.
choices: Training doctors to work in hospitals on Earth
Producing medicine for sale to other countries
Testing systems for possible future space missions
Providing homes for visitors traveling to Mars
Replacing all scientific laboratories on Earth
solution: ISS에서는 미래의 달, 화성, 소행성 탐사에 필요할 수 있는 우주선 시스템을 시험한다고 했다. 따라서 미래 우주 임무를 위한 시스템 시험이라는 ③이 알맞다.

body:
다음 글의 필자가 우주 유영 중 실제로 한 행동은?

I left the airlock with Scott to fit supports for new solar batteries outside the station. After entering space, I attached my safety cable to a ring near the airlock. We then followed the handrail toward the station’s edge. Although I was frightened by the darkness ahead, I eventually finished installing the supports.
choices: He attached his safety cable to a ring.
He waited inside while Scott completed the installation.
He removed the old solar batteries from the airlock.
He let go of the handrail to return to Earth.
He stopped the mission before installing the supports.
solution: 필자는 우주로 나온 뒤 에어록 근처의 고리에 안전 케이블을 연결했다고 했다. 두려움을 느끼기는 했지만 설치 작업은 끝냈으므로 ⑤는 틀리다.

body:
다음 대화에 따르면, 누리호에 관해 답을 찾을 수 있는 질문은?

M: We have just heard the official news that the launch succeeded. What missions are planned for Nuri?
W: It will put satellites into orbit around Earth. Its missions also include observing the ground and space weather.
M: Was the rocket developed with Korean technology?
W: Yes. It was developed domestically, making this an important achievement for Korea.
choices: How much did the rocket cost to develop?
How long will each satellite remain in orbit?
Who first suggested the rocket’s name?
What kinds of observations are included in its missions?
On what date did construction of the rocket begin?
solution: 대화에는 누리호의 임무에 지상 관측과 우주 기상 관측이 포함된다고 나와 있다. 개발 비용, 위성의 궤도 체류 기간, 이름 제안자, 제작 시작 날짜는 제시되지 않았다.

body:
다음 글을 바탕으로 필자의 경험을 이해한 내용 중 적절하지 않은 것은?

As Scott and I emerged from the airlock, Earth appeared above us like an enormous blue dome. It almost seemed about to fall toward us. I made myself concentrate on the installation and connected my safety cable to a ring. Farther along the handrail, the apparently limitless darkness made me afraid of losing my grip, even with the cable attached. Once the supports were in place, I looked back at Earth and was struck by its extraordinary beauty.
choices: Earth initially gave the writer the impression that it might fall toward him.
Attaching the safety cable completely removed the writer’s fear.
The writer deliberately directed his attention to the work.
The writer worried about losing his hold while moving along the handrail.
The writer admired Earth after completing the installation.
solution: 필자는 안전 케이블을 연결한 상태에서도 손잡이를 놓칠까 봐 두려워했다. 따라서 케이블 연결이 두려움을 완전히 없앴다는 ②는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.

body:
다음 글을 읽은 학생의 반응으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Building the ISS required cooperation among many nations over a long period. Thousands of participants brought different languages, engineering methods, and standards to the project. Spacewalkers assembled its parts in a vacuum while facing extreme temperatures. The station now supports research and the testing of systems for possible future exploration. Many astronauts regard it as evidence of what people can accomplish together.
choices: “The project succeeded because every participant already used identical engineering standards.”
“The station’s value is limited to providing a place for astronauts to live.”
“The assembly work took place under conditions similar to those on Earth.”

Is it impossible to build an environment where everyone can use products and facilities conveniently and without limitations? It was Ronald Mace who sought the answer to this question. He contracted polio at the age of nine and spent the rest of his life in a wheelchair. When studying architecture at university, he struggled to access some campus facilities due to inaccessible building designs. This experience later inspired him to invent the term universal design, which refers to design for all. As an architect and product designer, he pursued a world in which all products and environments were designed to be artistic and usable to the greatest extent possible by everyone, regardless of their age, size, disability, nationality, or language.

In addition, it should be cognitively accessible and minimize users’ physical efforts. Finally, it requires the providing of sufficient space for all users while reducing potential hazards and adverse consequences from accidental or unintended actions. A key feature of universal design is that this is not a special requirement only for the benefit of a minority of the population. If an environment is accessible, usable, convenient, and a pleasure to use, everyone in the community benefits.
How has universal design been incorporated into modern architecture? One of the most representative examples of universal design being used to improve accessibility is the ramps installed in front of buildings. Ramps, not stairs, are necessary for people with disabilities who use wheelchairs, and they are also beneficial for parents pushing strollers and the elderly.

Have you heard, “Hello, guys; let’s get started,” at the beginning of a meeting? Could that make some feel less included? Saying, “Hello, everyone,” instead of, “Hello, guys,” demonstrates inclusivity, reduces potential barriers, and enhances everyone’s sense of belonging. Inclusive language promotes equality, respect, and diversity, inviting all people to participate in society. For example, replacing conventional terms with racial implications like “blacklist” and “whitelist” with neutral alternatives such as “deny list” and “allow list” enhances inclusivity. Similarly, using gender-neutral terms like “parent” and “guardian” instead of “mom” and “dad” helps break down biases and acknowledges diverse family structures. Moreover, it is crucial to be aware of everyday phrases that could be considered insensitive toward individuals with medical conditions. For instance, using “missed opportunity” instead of “blind spot” or “ridiculous” rather than “crazy” demonstrates more thoughtful communication.

This experience later inspired him to invent the term universal design, which refers to design for all. solution: (a)는 손이 가득 찬 어른과 문을 열기에 키가 작은 아이들, (b)는 보도·계단·횡단보도, (d)는 도시 공간에서 길을 안내해 준다는 내용으로 답할 수 있다. (c) 자동문이 처음 설치된 시기는 글에 나오지 않는다. (e) 글에서는 점자 블록을 ‘textured surfaces(표면이 울퉁불퉁한 바닥)’라고만 했을 뿐 재료는 밝히지 않았으므로 답할 수 없다. 따라서 정답은 (a), (b), (d)이다.

body:
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Beth: The stock market is an official place (A)[which / where] you can buy and sell shares in a company. Many people believe (B)[that / what] investing is a good way to build wealth. However, it is important (C)[remembering / to remember] that there is always a risk of loss and debt.
choices: where – that – to remember
which – that – remembering
where – what – to remember
which – what – remembering
where – that – remembering
solution: 선행사 place가 장소이고 뒤에 완전한 절이 오므로 관계부사 where가 알맞다. believe 뒤에 완전한 절을 이끄는 접속사는 that이다. 'it is important' 뒤의 진주어 자리에는 to부정사 to remember가 와야 한다. 따라서 정답은 ①.

body:
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

Neil: Thank you for ⓐtuning in. We ⓑhave been talking about the world of stocks. Investing ⓒis challenging, but it can also be rewarding. I think many people ⓓfind the stock market confusing. I bet all our listeners ⓔhas asked themselves the same question.
solution: ⓔ의 주어 all our listeners는 복수이므로 동사는 has가 아니라 have가 되어야 한다. ⓐ는 전치사 for의 목적어인 동명사, ⓑ는 현재완료진행형, ⓒ는 동명사 주어에 대한 단수 동사 is, ⓓ는 복수 주어 people에 맞는 동사로 모두 올바르다. 따라서 어색한 것은 ⑤.

body:
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Beth: Let's imagine a small company (A)[produces / producing] innovative sneakers. There are (B)[so / such] many investors interested in it. When the company (C)[lists / is listed] on the stock market, individuals can buy shares and become partial owners.
choices: producing – so – is listed
produces – so – lists
producing – such – is listed
produces – such – lists
producing – so – lists
solution: (A)는 a company를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사구로, 회사가 '생산하는' 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 producing이 알맞다. (B)는 복수명사 investors를 수식하므로 'so many'가 맞고 'such many'는 쓸 수 없다. (C)는 회사가 '상장되는' 수동 관계이므로 is listed가 되어야 한다. 따라서 정답은 ①.

body:
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Beth: A bear market is a stock market situation (A)[which / in which] stock values decline. Factors like low GDP growth and rising unemployment are (B)[possible / possibly] conditions for a bear market. In difficult economic situations, investors have negative views, which may lead them (C)[to sell / selling] their stocks.
choices: which – possible – to sell
in which – possibly – selling
in which – possible – to sell
which – possibly – selling
in which – possible – selling
solution: (A)는 뒤에 완전한 절(stock values decline)이 오므로 '전치사+관계대명사'인 in which가 알맞다. (B)는 명사 conditions를 수식하는 자리이므로 형용사 possible이 와야 한다. (C)는 'lead+목적어+to부정사' 구문이므로 to sell이 맞다. 따라서 정답은 ③.

body:
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

Beth: The more successful a business ⓐis, the more people ⓑwill buy its stocks. As demand for the stocks increases, ⓒso the stock price does. Companies are also under the influence of various market factors ⓓaffecting the price. For example, if the price of rubber ⓔwill rise, a shoe company may have to pay more to import it.
solution: ⓒ는 '~도 또한 그렇다'의 뜻으로 'so+동사+주어'의 도치 어순이어야 하므로 so does the stock price가 되어야 한다. ⓔ는 조건을 나타내는 if절이므로 미래 대신 현재시제 rises를 써야 한다. ⓐ(the 비교급 구문의 동사), ⓑ(주절의 미래), ⓓ(factors를 수식하는 현재분사)는 모두 올바르다. 따라서 어색한 것은 ⓒ, ⓔ로 정답은 ③.

body:
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 어법상 알맞지 않은 것은?

Beth: In purchasing such stocks, investors ⓐnot only pursue their financial goals but also contribute to building a more sustainable system. As demand for the stocks increases, ⓑso does the stock price. Companies are under the influence of market factors ⓒaffecting the price. If a company performs disappointingly, its stock price falls, ⓓleading to a decline in value. The stock market is important because it provides companies with the money ⓔthey need to grow.
choices: ⓐ: contribute to building a more sustainable system as well as pursue their financial goals
ⓑ: the stock price increases, too
ⓒ: which affect the price
ⓓ: which leads to a decline in value
ⓔ: what they need to grow
solution: ⓔ는 선행사 the money가 있으므로 관계대명사 what은 쓸 수 없고 that(또는 which)만 가능하므로 'what they need to grow'로의 전환은 틀렸다. ⓐ는 'not only A but also B'를 'B as well as A'로 바르게 전환했고, ⓑ는 도치문의 의미를 그대로 풀어 썼으며, ⓒ는 복수 선행사 factors에 맞는 복수 동사 affect를 썼고, ⓓ는 앞 절 전체를 받는 계속적 용법 which leads로 바르게 전환했다. 따라서 알맞지 않은 것은 ⑤.

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Beth: Let's start with the concept of a stock. A stock is a partial share of ownership in a company. When you buy a stock, you get a portion of the company's ownership. To put it simply, owning one stock is like having a slice of the company's pie.
Neil: Does that mean stockholders themselves can actively participate in the management of the company?
Beth: Not exactly, Neil. Management is generally carried out by professional managers. However, companies hold stockholder meetings to seek the opinions of major stockholders when they make important decisions.
choices: A stock is a partial share of ownership in a company.
Buying a stock gives you a portion of the company's ownership.
Owning one stock is compared to having a slice of the company's pie.
A company's management is usually handled by professional managers.
Stockholders personally take charge of running the company every day.
solution: 지문에서 경영은 일반적으로 전문 경영인이 맡는다고 했으므로 주주가 직접 매일 회사를 운영한다는 ⑤는 일치하지 않는다. ①②③은 주식의 개념 설명과, ④는 경영 주체 설명과 일치한다. 회사는 중요한 결정 시 주요 주주의 의견을 듣기 위해 주주 총회를 열 뿐이다.

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

A bull market is a rising stock market situation in which economic conditions are favorable to investors. These include high employment rates, GDP increases, and other positive economic indicators. In a bull market, investors increase their stock purchases and maintain their investments. In contrast, a bear market implies a decline in stock values. It occurs when economic conditions are not favorable, and most stocks experience decreases in value. Factors like low GDP growth, rising unemployment, and low wages are possible conditions for a bear market. In difficult economic situations, investors frequently have negative views of the stock market, which may lead them to sell their stocks.
choices: In a bull market, economic conditions are favorable to investors.
High employment rates and GDP increases are signs of a bull market.
In a bear market, most stocks experience decreases in value.
Low GDP growth and rising unemployment can bring about a bear market.
During a bear market, investors increase their stock purchases and hold on to their investments.
solution: 약세장(bear market)에서는 투자자들이 주식 시장을 부정적으로 보고 주식을 '파는' 경향이 있다. 주식 구매를 늘리고 투자를 유지하는 것은 강세장(bull market)의 특징이므로 ⑤가 일치하지 않는다. ①②는 강세장, ③④는 약세장 설명과 일치한다.

body:
위 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

G: Hey, have you ever bought anything from a resale market?
B: Yeah. I got a great deal on some limited-release sneakers through an online resale market. I'm happy with buying from resale platforms because I was able to get such unique sneakers at a reasonable price.
G: I've tried shopping on those sites, but I'm worried about the condition and the quality of the used products.
B: I understand. But the sneakers I got were in excellent condition. Just make sure to choose a resale platform with high ratings and check the seller's reputation and product pictures before purchasing anything.
G: Right. Thank you for your advice.
choices: The boy bought limited-release sneakers through an online resale market.
The boy got the sneakers at a reasonable price.
The girl has never shopped on resale sites before.
The sneakers the boy bought were in excellent condition.
The boy advises checking the seller's reputation and product pictures before buying.
solution: 소녀는 "I've tried shopping on those sites"라고 말해 재판매 사이트에서 쇼핑해 본 적이 있다고 했으므로, 한 번도 이용한 적이 없다는 ③은 일치하지 않는다. ①②④⑤는 소년의 구매 경험과 조언 내용과 일치한다.

body:
윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

Beth: The stock market is very important for companies because it can provide them with the money they need to grow and expand. Let's imagine that a small group of people start a footwear company that produces innovative sneakers. The founders are confident that their products will be popular with consumers, but they do not have enough funds to grow the business. So they decide to put the newly formed company on the stock market. When a company is listed on the stock market, individuals or organizations that believe in the company's bright future can buy shares and become partial owners of the company. This process makes it easy for the footwear company to raise the funds it needs to grow its business. As the business grows, the stock value rises, and the stockholders' profits increase.
choices: Why is the stock market important for companies?
What does the footwear company produce?
What were the founders lacking despite their confidence in the products?
How much money did the footwear company raise after being listed?
Who becomes a partial owner when a company is listed on the stock market?
solution: 지문은 회사가 상장되면 자금을 쉽게 조달할 수 있다고만 말할 뿐, 신발 회사가 실제로 얼마의 자금을 모았는지는 언급하지 않으므로 ④는 답할 수 없다. ①은 성장·확장 자금 제공, ②는 혁신적 운동화, ③은 사업 성장 자금 부족, ⑤는 주식을 산 개인·기관이 부분 소유자가 된다는 내용으로 모두 답할 수 있다.

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Beth: Investors may be concerned about a company's leadership or reputation. Nowadays, more and more people are starting to support companies that prioritize public values such as business transparency, environmental friendliness, and social justice. In purchasing such stocks, they not only pursue their financial goals but also contribute to building a more sustainable economic system that benefits the entire society. All these variables can cause daily changes in stock prices in the stock market.
choices: Investors may take a company's leadership or reputation into account.
An increasing number of people support companies that value public values like social justice.
Buying stocks of companies with public values can help build a more sustainable economic system.
People who buy such stocks give up their own financial goals for the sake of society.
Various factors can lead to daily changes in stock prices.
solution: 지문에서 공적 가치를 중시하는 기업의 주식을 사는 사람들은 재정적 목표를 '추구하면서 동시에(not only ~ but also)' 지속 가능한 경제에 기여한다고 했다. 따라서 재정적 목표를 포기한다는 ④는 일치하지 않는다. ①②③⑤는 각각 리더십·평판 고려, 공적 가치 기업 지지 증가, 지속 가능한 경제 기여, 주가의 일일 변동 요인과 일치한다.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

When a company wants to grow but does not have enough money, it can sell small parts of itself to the public. By listing itself on the stock market, the company allows people who believe in its future to buy shares and become partial owners. In return, the company receives the funds it needs to expand its business. As the company grows and earns more, the value of its shares rises, and the people who bought them share in the profit.
choices: how a company raises funds by listing on the stock market
reasons why new companies fail to attract any investors
the process of choosing a good professional manager
risks of borrowing money from a bank to grow a business
how stockholders take part in daily company management
solution: 글은 회사가 자금이 부족할 때 주식 시장에 상장하여 사람들에게 주식을 팔아 성장 자금을 마련하는 과정을 설명한다. 투자자는 부분 소유자가 되고 회사가 성장하면 함께 이익을 얻는다. 따라서 주제는 '회사가 주식 시장 상장을 통해 자금을 마련하는 방법'인 ①이다. ③·⑤는 글의 핵심이 아닌 지엽적 내용이다.

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

The mood of the stock market can change greatly over time. When the economy is strong and people feel hopeful, they buy more shares and prices keep climbing. On the other hand, when the economy weakens and people lose confidence, they sell their shares and prices fall. Knowing which mood the market is in helps investors decide when to buy or sell.
choices: The History of the World's Largest Stock Exchanges
Rising and Falling Moods That Move the Stock Market
Simple Tricks to Always Make a Profit on Stocks
Why Teenagers Should Avoid Buying Any Shares
The Daily Life of a Professional Fund Manager
solution: 글은 경제 상황과 사람들의 심리에 따라 주식 시장 분위기가 오르기도 내리기도 한다는 내용을 다룬다. 상승·하락이라는 두 흐름이 핵심이므로 제목은 ②가 가장 알맞다. ③·④는 글에 근거가 없고 ①·⑤는 지문과 무관하다.

body:
다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?

Many people think that putting money into stocks is a quick and easy way to get rich. In reality, the market goes up and down all the time, so there is always a chance of losing money. Before you invest, you should study the companies carefully, keep up with news about them, and only risk what you can afford to lose. Being careful and well informed matters far more than being lucky.
choices: 투자할 때는 신중함과 정보 습득이 무엇보다 중요하다.
주식은 누구나 쉽게 부자가 될 수 있는 방법이다.
은행 예금이 주식보다 항상 더 많은 이익을 준다.
운이 좋으면 손해 없이 큰돈을 벌 수 있다.
뉴스를 보지 않아도 좋은 회사를 고를 수 있다.
solution: 글은 주식 투자가 쉬운 돈벌이라는 생각과 달리 늘 손실 위험이 있으므로, 회사를 공부하고 정보를 챙기며 감당할 수 있는 돈만 투자하라고 조언한다. 마지막 문장에서 '운보다 신중함과 정보가 더 중요하다'고 못 박으므로 요지는 ①이다. ②·④는 글이 반박하는 통념이다.

body:
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

The price of a stock moves according to supply and demand. When a company does well, more people want to own a piece of it, so they rush to buy its shares. As this demand grows, the price goes up. But if a company performs poorly, people lose interest, the demand falls, and the price drops.

[요약문]
A stock's price depends on supply and demand. When a company succeeds, demand (A)________ and the price goes up; when it performs poorly, demand falls and the price (B)________.
choices: rises – declines
rises – climbs
falls – declines
falls – climbs
stays – declines
solution: 회사가 잘되면 수요가 '증가(rises)'하여 가격이 오르고, 실적이 나쁘면 수요가 줄어 가격이 '하락(declines)'한다. 따라서 (A)는 rises, (B)는 declines인 ①이 정답이다. ②·④의 climbs는 가격 상승을 뜻해 문맥과 반대다.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

A stock is a small share of ownership in a company. When you buy one, you own a tiny part of that business, much like owning a single slice of a large pie. However, owning a share does not mean you run the company. Daily decisions are made by professional managers. Still, companies hold meetings to hear the opinions of their major shareholders when important decisions must be made.
choices: what a stock is and the limited role of shareholders
the daily duties of a company's professional managers
the best strategies for buying many different stocks
the reasons companies hold shareholder meetings every day
how to calculate the total value of a company's pie
solution: 글은 주식이 회사 소유권의 일부라는 정의와 함께, 주주가 경영을 직접 하지는 않지만 중요한 결정 때 의견을 묻는다는 제한된 역할을 설명한다. 따라서 주제는 '주식의 정의와 주주의 제한된 역할'인 ①이다. ④는 매일 회의를 연다고 과장해 글과 어긋난다.

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

A stock's price is shaped by far more than how well a company sells its products. Market factors such as the cost of raw materials, new production technology, and workers' wages all play a part. For example, if the price of rubber rises, a shoe maker must pay more to produce sneakers, which pushes up prices and may hurt sales. These days, investors also care about a company's values, choosing to support businesses that are honest, protect the environment, and treat society fairly.
choices: Why Rubber Prices Decide the Future of Shoe Makers
The Many Forces That Shape a Company's Stock Price
A Simple Guide to Building an Eco-friendly Company
Step-by-step Methods for Selling Sneakers Abroad
The One Golden Rule Every Investor Must Always Follow
solution: 글은 원자재 값·생산 기술·임금 같은 시장 요인에 더해 기업의 가치관까지 주가에 영향을 준다는 여러 요인을 폭넓게 다룬다. 따라서 제목은 '주가를 움직이는 다양한 요인'인 ②가 알맞다. ①은 고무·신발이라는 예시 하나에 치우친 함정 선지이고, ③은 본문의 한 부분(가치관)만 확대한 오답이며 ④·⑤는 글에 근거가 없다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 < > 안의 단어를 바르게 배열하시오.

Now I’m getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I’m still often confused about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I’m upside down. Of course, it’s actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. (A)나는 어떤 벽이든 마치 각각이 바닥인 것처럼 똑같이 사용할 수 있다. Everything has zero weight.

< each / any wall / I / a floor / use / were / can / as if / equally >

______________________________________________.
answer: I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor.
solution: ‘마치 ~인 것처럼’은 현재 사실과 반대되는 일을 가정하는 ‘as if + 주어 + 동사의 과거형’으로 나타냅니다. 가정법 과거이므로 be동사는 주어와 상관없이 were를 씁니다. 부사 equally는 목적어 any wall 뒤에 둡니다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 < > 안의 단어 및 어구를 바르게 배열하시오.

Day 100 The Descent to Earth
Mother Earth didn’t exactly welcome us back with open arms. (A)지구의 대기는 우주로부터 들어오는 물체들에 저항력이 있다. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat.

< entering / is / objects / Earth’s atmosphere / to / resistant / from space >

______________________________________________.
answer: Earth’s atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space.
solution: ‘~에 저항력이 있다’는 be resistant to로 나타냅니다. ‘우주로부터 들어오는 물체들’은 현재분사구 entering from space가 objects를 뒤에서 꾸미는 형태입니다. 물체가 스스로 들어오는 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사 entering을 씁니다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말과 뜻이 같도록 <조건>에 맞게 < > 안의 단어 및 어구를 바르게 배열하시오.

It’s hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. (A)내 팔은 끔찍하게 무겁게 느껴졌고, 내 다리도 그랬다. Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time. The important thing is I’m home.

<조건> • ‘so + 동사 + 주어’ 구문을 사용할 것 • 단어를 추가하거나 빼지 말 것

< so / my arms / heavy / did / felt / my legs / terribly / and >

______________________________________________.
answer: My arms felt terribly heavy, and so did my legs.
solution: ‘감각동사 felt + 형용사 보어 heavy’ 앞에 부사 terribly를 넣어 앞 절을 만듭니다. ‘~도 그렇다’는 ‘so + 동사 + 주어’ 도치로 나타냅니다. 앞 절의 동사가 일반동사의 과거형 felt이므로 대동사 did를 써서 so did my legs가 됩니다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하여 문장을 완성하시오.

The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us. (A)나 자신이 그 작업에 집중하도록 억지로 만들면서, 나는 내 안전줄의 고리를 에어록 바로 바깥의 고리에 고정했다. We moved along the handrail to the edge of the station.

<조건> • 분사구문을 사용할 것 • ‘force + 목적어 + to부정사’ 구문을 사용할 것 • <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것) • 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기> force, myself, focus on, the task, secure, the hook, safety cable, a ring

_____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____, _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ just outside the airlock.
answer: Forcing myself to focus on the task, I secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring
solution: 주절의 주어 I와 같은 주어를 생략하고, 동시동작을 나타내는 분사구문 Forcing ~으로 시작합니다. 주어와 목적어가 같으므로 재귀대명사 myself를 쓰고, ‘force + 목적어 + to부정사’에 따라 to focus on the task를 이어 씁니다. 주절은 ‘secure A to B(A를 B에 고정하다)’ 구조로 동사를 과거형 secured로 바꿉니다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하여 문장을 완성하시오.

Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time. The important thing is I’m home. I can smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! (A)나는 이것들이 얼마나 마법 같은지를 내 남은 평생 동안 기억할 것이다.

<조건> • 간접의문문을 사용할 것 • <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것) • 앞에 주어진 어구를 제외하고 12단어로 쓸 것
<보기> remember, how, magical, these things, be, for, the rest, life

I’ll ______________________________________________.
answer: remember how magical these things are for the rest of my life
solution: remember의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문은 ‘의문사 + 주어 + 동사’ 순서이고, how가 형용사를 수식하므로 how magical 뒤에 these things are를 씁니다. 주어가 복수이므로 be는 are로 바꿉니다. ‘남은 평생 동안’은 for the rest of my life이며, 이렇게 쓰면 정확히 12단어입니다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하여 문장을 완성하시오.

It’s hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt terribly heavy, and so did my legs. (A)우주에서 내가 그리워했던 중력에 익숙해지는 것은 꽤 오랜 시간이 걸릴 것이다. The important thing is I’m home.

<조건> • 동명사구 주어를 사용할 것 • 계속적 용법의 관계대명사를 사용할 것 • <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 모두 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것) • 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기> get, use, to, gravity, which, miss, in space, take, quite, long, time

_____ _____ _____ _____, _____ _____ _____ _____ _____, _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____.
answer: Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time
solution: ‘~에 익숙해지다’는 ‘get used to + (동)명사’이고, 문장의 주어가 되도록 동명사 Getting used to gravity로 바꿉니다. 이때 ‘used to + 동사원형(~하곤 했다)’과 헷갈리지 않도록 주의합니다. 콤마 사이에는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사절 which I missed in space를 넣습니다. 동명사 주어는 단수 취급하며, 어순은 ‘quite + a + 형용사 + 명사’이므로 will take quite a long time이 됩니다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하여 문장을 완성하시오.

Mother Earth didn’t exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth’s atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. (A)이것은, 그렇지 않으면 지구 위로 비처럼 쏟아져 내릴 궤도 잔해로부터 지구를 보호한다. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.

<조건> • ‘protect A from B’ 구문을 사용할 것 • 주격 관계대명사 that을 사용할 것 • 가정의 의미를 나타내는 조동사와 otherwise를 사용할 것 • <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것) • 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기> protect, the planet, from, the orbital debris, that, would, otherwise, rain down, on it

This _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____ _____.
answer: protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it
solution: 주어 This가 3인칭 단수이고 일반적인 사실을 말하므로 protect는 protects로 씁니다. ‘protect A from B’ 구문에 따라 the planet from the orbital debris로 이어 쓰고, 선행사 the orbital debris를 주격 관계대명사 that절이 꾸밉니다. ‘그렇지 않으면 ~할 것이다’는 대기가 없다고 가정한 내용이므로 ‘would + otherwise + 동사원형’ 순서로 써서 would otherwise rain down on it이 됩니다.

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?

The successful use of sports analytics was not limited to the curling team. The Korean women's archery team had dominated the sport for decades. However, the team turned to sports analytics to maintain its edge over its rivals in preparation for the 2020 Tokyo Olympics. The team developed a system to monitor players' heart rates by using advanced visual computing technology to convert facial color variations into heart rates. This data was used for psychological training to help players maintain stable heart rates during crucial moments. The team also created an AI coach that helped adjust shooting form. The team managers requested that the AI coach edit training videos of the players to assist with practical analysis. Players and coaches used the edited videos to analyze the players' usual habits or weaknesses. The active use of data analysis by the Korean women's archery team handed them their ninth Olympic gold medal in a row in Tokyo.
choices: The History of Archery as an Olympic Sport
How Data Analysis Helped Korean Archers Keep Winning
Why Heart Rates Rise During Crucial Moments
AI Coaches Replacing Human Coaches in Archery
The Growing Rivalry Between Korean and Foreign Archery Teams
solution: 한국 여자 양궁팀은 정상의 자리를 지키려고 심박수 측정 시스템과 AI 코치 같은 데이터 분석을 도입했고, 그 결과 올림픽 9연속 금메달을 따냈다는 내용이다. 따라서 '데이터 분석이 한국 양궁 선수들의 연승을 어떻게 도왔는가'가 제목으로 알맞다. ③은 세부 내용의 일부일 뿐이고, ④의 'AI 코치가 인간 코치를 대체한다'는 내용은 글에 없다.

body:
다음 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Following its debut at the Winter Olympic Games of 2014, the Korean women's curling team recognized the need to enhance its sweeping technique. Sweeping melts the ice and makes the stone move faster. If too much ice melts, however, the stone moves too fast and misses the target. On the other hand, if not enough ice melts, the stone stops before reaching the target. The amount of ice melting depends on the sweeping speed and pressure. Applying too much pressure slows down the sweeping speed, and focusing only on speed makes it hard to transfer enough force to the broom. Finding the right balance between speed and pressure is important to melt the right amount of ice.
choices: 컬링에서는 얼음을 많이 녹일수록 스톤이 목표에 정확히 도달한다.
스위핑할 때 속도와 압력의 균형을 잘 맞춰야 얼음을 알맞게 녹일 수 있다.
스위핑에서는 속도보다 압력에 집중하는 것이 더 효과적이다.
올림픽에 처음 출전한 경험은 선수들의 기술 향상에 큰 도움이 된다.
컬링 스톤의 속도는 얼음이 녹는 양과 관계가 없다.
solution: 얼음이 너무 많이 녹아도, 너무 적게 녹아도 스톤이 목표에서 벗어나므로, 마지막 문장처럼 속도와 압력 사이의 균형을 찾는 것이 중요하다는 것이 이 글의 요지이다. ①과 ⑤는 글의 내용과 반대이다. ③은 한쪽에만 집중하면 문제가 생긴다는 글의 내용과 맞지 않는다.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?

The data team of the Liverpool Football Club started to apply data analysis in key areas of club management, including player recruitment, injury prevention, and strategy during the game. The team analyzed large amounts of data to recruit players who fit the team's style of play. In training, they collected data on players' movement patterns, heart rates, and vital signs by using GPS trackers and sensors to prevent injuries. During games, they used live data to make tactical decisions such as substitutions and formations.
choices: ways Liverpool's data team used data in various areas of the club
the importance of GPS trackers in professional soccer matches
reasons why players' heart rates change during training
the history of tactical formations in modern soccer
difficulties of recruiting players with limited funds
solution: 첫 문장에서 데이터 분석을 선수 영입, 부상 예방, 경기 중 전략에 적용했다고 밝힌 뒤, 나머지 문장에서 각 영역의 활용 방법을 하나씩 설명한다. 따라서 '리버풀 데이터팀이 구단의 여러 영역에서 데이터를 활용한 방법'이 주제이다. ②와 ③은 부상 예방 부분의 세부 내용에 그친다.

body:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?

In soccer, the Liverpool Football Club of the English Premier League is similar to the Oakland Athletics in baseball. In 2010, Liverpool underwent a change in ownership. While data analysis was already prevailing in the Premier League at that time, the new owner of the club, who also owned a baseball team in the United States, aimed to push data analysis in soccer to new heights. So he demanded that the club form a new data team.
The new team included a physicist from Cambridge, a nuclear scientist from Harvard, and a former chess champion. What they had in common was significant expertise in data. The team started to apply data analysis in key areas of club management, including player recruitment, injury prevention, and strategy during the game. (…) The data team was praised for its efforts when the Liverpool Football Club won the league championship for the first time in 30 years in 2020.

→ Under its new owner, Liverpool formed a data team with great (A)__________ in data, and the team's use of data analysis in club management (B)__________ to the club's first league title in 30 years.
choices: (A) expertise …… (B) contributed
(A) experience …… (B) objected
(A) indifference …… (B) led
(A) expertise …… (B) objected
(A) ignorance …… (B) contributed
solution: 데이터팀 구성원들의 공통점은 'significant expertise in data'였으므로 (A)에는 expertise(전문 지식)가 알맞다. 데이터팀은 리버풀의 30년 만의 리그 우승에 대한 공로로 칭찬받았으므로 (B)에는 contributed (to)(~에 기여했다)가 알맞다. indifference(무관심), ignorance(무지)는 글의 내용과 반대이고, objected (to)(반대했다)는 흐름에 맞지 않는다.

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

The Oakland Athletics were a Major League Baseball team with a small budget and limited funds. Because of this, it was hard for them to attract talented players. However, in 2002, they surprised the professional sports industry by winning 20 games in a row. The secret behind their success was sabermetrics, a statistical model used for making decisions in baseball.
choices: The Oakland Athletics did not have much money to spend.
Their limited funds made it difficult to attract talented players.
In 2002, the team won 20 consecutive games.
The professional sports industry had expected the team's success in advance.
Sabermetrics is a statistical model used for decision-making in baseball.
solution: 본문은 2002년 20연승이 프로 스포츠계를 '놀라게 했다(surprised/shocked)'고 했으므로, 그 성공을 미리 '예상했다'는 ④는 반대되는 내용이다. ①②③⑤는 본문 내용과 일치한다.

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

To find the most effective sweeping technique, the Korean curling team designed a special measurement device. The device was made up of infrared cameras and sensors attached to the players' bodies, shoes, and brooms. Using the device, the team obtained foot pressure values and other data for analysis. After studying the data, they concluded that speed was more economical than strength for sweeping. This use of data analysis helped the team win a silver medal at the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics.
choices: The Korean team built a device to discover the best sweeping technique.
Sensors were attached to the players' bodies as well as their shoes and brooms.
Foot pressure values were among the data gathered for analysis.
The team found that using strength was more economical than increasing speed.
Data analysis contributed to the team's silver medal at the 2018 Pyeongchang Olympics.
solution: 본문은 스위핑에서 '힘보다 속도(speed)가 더 경제적'이라고 결론 내렸으므로, '힘이 속도보다 경제적'이라고 뒤바꾼 ④가 일치하지 않는다. 나머지는 모두 본문과 일치한다.

body:
윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

A baseball has 108 double stitches, which create raised lines called seams. The seams help pitchers grip the ball and add more spin when they throw it. A spinning ball changes direction in the air because of the air pressure around it, an effect known as the Magnus effect. As for the bat, its length must be less than 106.8 cm, and the diameter of its thickest part must be less than 7 cm. If a batter hits the ball about 5-10 cm from the end of the bat, the ball flies the farthest. This spot is called the "sweet spot."
choices: How many double stitches does a baseball have?
What effect causes a spinning ball to change direction in the air?
What is the maximum allowed length of a baseball bat?
How much does a regulation baseball weigh?
How far from the end of the bat is the sweet spot located?
solution: ① 108개, ② 마그누스 효과, ③ 106.8cm 미만, ⑤ 끝에서 5~10cm 지점으로 모두 본문에서 답을 찾을 수 있다. 그러나 공의 '무게'에 대한 언급은 전혀 없으므로 ④는 답할 수 없다.

body:
윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

In 2010, the Liverpool Football Club went through a change in ownership. The new owner, who also owned a baseball team in the United States, wanted to raise data analysis in soccer to a new level, so he demanded that the club form a new data team. The team included a physicist from Cambridge, a nuclear scientist from Harvard, and a former chess champion, all of whom had great expertise in data. They applied data analysis to player recruitment, injury prevention, and in-game strategy. During training, they used GPS trackers and sensors to collect data on players' movements, heart rates, and vital signs. The club won the league championship in 2020, its first in 30 years.
choices: In what year did Liverpool's ownership change?
What did the members of the new data team have in common?
In which areas of club management was data analysis applied?
What tools were used to collect players' data during training?
How much salary did the new owner pay the data team members?
solution: ① 2010년, ② 데이터에 대한 전문성, ③ 선수 영입·부상 예방·경기 중 전략, ④ GPS 추적기와 센서로 모두 본문에서 확인된다. 그러나 데이터 팀에게 지급한 '급여'는 본문에 전혀 나오지 않으므로 ⑤는 답할 수 없다.

body:
윗글을 읽고 추론한 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?

In soccer, players use numbers and other information to predict what might happen during penalty kicks. They analyze how the opposing team's players performed in the past, learning whether they scored or missed. Kickers also study the goalkeeper's previous movements to find patterns. For example, if the data shows that a goalkeeper often dives low to the left, the kicker may decide to aim high to the right to increase the chance of scoring.
choices: Analyzing data is useless when a kicker faces a goalkeeper for the first time.
A kicker is likely to aim the ball toward the direction the goalkeeper tends to avoid.
Goalkeepers always dive low to the left during penalty kicks.
Players rely only on their own past records, not on their opponents'.
The more a kicker ignores the data, the more likely he is to score.
solution: 골키퍼가 자주 왼쪽 아래로 몸을 날리면 키커는 반대인 오른쪽 위로 찬다는 예시에서, 키커는 골키퍼가 가지 않는(피하는) 방향을 노린다는 것을 추론할 수 있으므로 ②가 적절하다. ③은 'often'을 'always'로 과장했고, ④⑤와 ①은 데이터 활용 취지에 어긋난다.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

King Jeongjo's procession in 1795 had a special purpose. That year was his mother's sixtieth birthday, which had a special meaning in the Joseon Dynasty. Also, his father's tomb was near Hwaseong Haenggung, so the king planned to hold a memorial service there to honor his late father. the long history of royal tombs in Joseon
King Jeongjo's respect for his family shown through the procession
the role of musicians in royal ceremonies
the difficulty of traveling long distances in the past

While Hwaseong Fortress was being built, King Jeongjo treated the workers well. They received fair wages and were given breaks during bad weather. They were even paid when they were sick. Back then, ordinary people were usually required to work on public projects without getting paid, so this was very unusual.
choices: 화성 건설에는 동양과 서양의 건축 기술이 함께 쓰였다.
정조는 화성 건설에 참여한 노동자들을 공정하게 대우했다.
당시 백성이 공공사업에 무보수로 일하는 것은 당연한 의무였다.
나쁜 날씨 때문에 화성 공사가 자주 늦어졌다.
일할 사람이 부족해서 화성 공사 기간이 길어졌다.
solution: 공정한 임금, 궂은 날씨의 휴식, 아플 때의 임금 지급처럼 노동자를 잘 대우한 사례를 차례로 든 글이다. 따라서 요지는 ②이다. ③은 당시 관행을 설명하는 배경일 뿐 필자가 하려는 말이 아니다. ①, ④, ⑤는 이 글에 나오지 않는다.

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

King Jeongjo made detailed records of the procession and the construction of Hwaseong Fortress. When the fortress was damaged during wartime, these records became very useful. At first, people at UNESCO were not sure whether the restored fortress was authentic. However, after they compared translated documents with the restored fortress, they agreed that it had been restored just the way it was meant to be.
choices: Why Wars Destroy Cultural Heritage
How UNESCO Translates Old Documents
The Military Power of the Joseon Dynasty
Records That Brought a Fortress Back to Life
The Life of King Jeongjo's Mother
solution: 정조가 남긴 자세한 기록 덕분에 전쟁으로 훼손된 화성을 원래대로 복원했고, 그 진정성까지 인정받았다는 내용이다. 그러니 제목은 '요새를 되살린 기록'인 ④가 알맞다. ②는 '번역된 문서'라는 표현만 따온 오답이다.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

During the procession, King Jeongjo gave common people a chance to meet him and share their concerns. This was especially meaningful for those who couldn't read or write, because they had no other way to tell the king what was on their minds. The procession also opened the door to government jobs. At that time, exams to hire officials were held only every three years. By adding special exams during the procession, the king gave more people a shot at joining the government, which made it more diverse.
choices: the difficulty of passing government exams in Joseon
how the procession brought the king and government closer to ordinary people
the reasons many people in Joseon could not read or write
the king's plan to reduce the number of government officials
the role of soldiers in protecting the king during the procession
solution: 앞부분은 백성이 왕을 직접 만나 걱정을 말할 기회를, 뒷부분은 특별 시험으로 관직의 문을 넓힌 일을 다룬다. 두 내용을 모두 담은 ②가 주제이다. ①과 ③은 글에 나온 낱말(exams, read or write)을 이용한 부분적 오답이다. ④는 관리를 더 뽑았다는 글의 내용과 반대이다.

body:
다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

King Jeongjo hoped to make Hwaseong the new capital, away from the political chaos in Hanyang. He wanted it to be a self-sufficient city with a strong military, farming, and trade. He gathered the best talents, such as Jeong Yakyong, and let them use the finest architectural techniques of the East and the West. He also treated the workers fairly, so workers from all over the country rushed to join. As a result, the construction, which was expected to take about ten years, was completed within three years.

→ King Jeongjo's (A)________ plans for Hwaseong and his fair treatment of workers led to the fortress being finished much (B)________ than expected.

   (A)          (B)
choices: modest ― faster
careless ― sooner
ambitious ― faster
ambitious ― later
secret ― slower
solution: 정조는 화성을 자급자족하는 새 수도로 만들려는 큰 계획을 세웠으므로 (A)에는 ambitious(야심 찬)가 들어간다. 10년 예상 공사가 3년 안에 끝났으므로 (B)에는 faster가 알맞다. ④의 later는 결과와 반대이다. ①의 modest와 ②의 careless는 계획의 성격과 맞지 않는다.

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

In the past, Koreans built two main types of fortresses. A sanseong was built on a mountain, so defenders could fight from higher ground and push back enemies with fewer soldiers. However, living there was not practical because there was little farmland. An eupseong was built on flat land and was the center of daily life, but in times of war, people had to move to a nearby sanseong for safety. Suwon Hwaseong combined the strengths of both. Built along the slopes of Paldalsan Mountain, it had strong defenses and also served as a center for agriculture, commerce, and housing.
choices: Why Mountain Fortresses Were Better Than Flat-land Ones
The Daily Life of Farmers Living Outside Eupseong
Famous Battles Fought at Mountain Fortresses
Suwon Hwaseong: The Best of Two Fortress Styles
How to Visit UNESCO Heritage Sites in Korea
solution: 산성과 읍성의 장단점을 차례로 설명한 뒤, 수원 화성이 두 양식의 장점을 합쳤다는 결론으로 끝나는 글이다. 따라서 제목은 ④이다. ①은 산성에도 단점이 있다는 글의 내용과 맞지 않는다. ②와 ③은 글에 없거나 아주 작은 부분만 다룬다.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?

On February 9, 1795, a huge procession left Changdeokgung Palace. More than 2,000 soldiers, hundreds of horse riders, and 50 musicians marched with King Jeongjo and his mother, and they even crossed the Hangang River on a bridge made of 36 boats. But this was not just about putting on a show. The trip took place around his mother's sixtieth birthday, and the king also planned a memorial service for his late father, whose tomb was near Hwaseong Haenggung. At the same time, the king wore armor and sat on a horse while his soldiers marched in perfect order, as if to say, "We're ready to protect our land."
choices: the technique used to build a bridge of boats on the Hangang River
how King Jeongjo honored his late father with a memorial service
a royal event that carried both personal and political meaning
the king's attempt to show off his wealth through a fancy parade
the military training soldiers received before the procession
solution: 행차의 규모를 소개한 뒤, 이 행차가 단순한 볼거리가 아니었다고 말한다. 가족에 대한 공경이라는 개인적 의미와 조선의 힘을 과시하는 정치적 의미가 함께 있었다는 것이다. 그래서 두 목적을 모두 담은 ③이 주제이다. ②는 두 목적 가운데 하나만 다룬 함정이고, ④는 'not just about putting on a show'와 반대이다.

body:

Hello, listeners. Today, I'd like to share some great ways to enjoy our community's culture. First, attend local cultural events such as festivals, concerts, and exhibitions. Through these events, you can experience the living traditions and customs of our community. Next, visit museums, art galleries, and historical sites. They hold the key to understanding our past by displaying works that reflect our unique heritage. In these ways, you can discover the richness and beauty of our community's culture.

Museums and historical sites display works that reflect the community's unique heritage.
The speaker recommends reading history books at home as the best way to learn the culture.
Visiting historical sites helps people understand their community's past.

solution: 글쓴이는 문화를 경험하는 방법으로 축제·공연·전시 참여와 박물관·미술관·유적지 방문을 제시했다. 집에서 역사책을 읽는 것을 가장 좋은 방법으로 추천한다는 언급은 전혀 없으므로 ③이 일치하지 않는다. 나머지는 모두 본문에 근거한다.

They had no other way to tell the king what was on their minds, so this was a direct line to him. Through the procession, King Jeongjo also made government more accessible. solution: 본문에 따르면 정조는 행차 때 특별 시험을 '추가로' 치러 더 많은 사람에게 기회를 주었다. 시험 수를 줄였다는 ④는 본문과 반대되므로 일치하지 않는다. 나머지는 모두 본문에 명시되어 있다.

body:
윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

Back on February 9, 1795, something remarkable happened in front of Changdeokgung Palace, where King Jeongjo lived. A large crowd gathered to witness a very special procession. More than 2,000 soldiers, hundreds of horse riders, and many important officials marched alongside the king and his mother, with 50 musicians playing traditional instruments. When they crossed a bridge made of 36 boats on the Hangang River, it turned heads. Lasting four days and covering 68 kilometers, the procession made a round trip to Hwaseong Haenggung.
choices: When did the procession take place?
About how many soldiers took part in the procession?
How was the bridge across the Hangang River made?
How many days did the procession last?
What kinds of traditional instruments did the 50 musicians play?
solution: 날짜(1795년 2월 9일), 군사 수(2,000명 이상), 다리(배 36척), 기간(4일)은 모두 본문에서 확인된다. 그러나 50명의 악사가 '어떤' 전통 악기를 연주했는지는 언급되지 않으므로 ⑤는 답할 수 없다.

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Suwon Hwaseong blends two Korean styles: the mountain fortress, or sanseong, and the flat-land fortress, or eupseong. The sanseong served as the final defense against invaders by using Korea's mountainous landscape. Defenders could fight from higher ground and push back enemies with fewer soldiers. However, living in the sanseong was not practical because of scarce farmland and poor living conditions. So during peaceful times, people lived in and around the eupseong, which had low walls and housed administrative buildings, learning centers, and training grounds. Common people, mainly farmers, lived outside these walls. In times of war, they withdrew to the nearby sanseong for safety.
choices: The sanseong used the mountainous landscape as a defensive advantage.
Defenders in the sanseong could push back enemies with fewer soldiers.
Living in the sanseong was difficult because of limited farmland.
During peaceful times, farmers lived inside the walls of the eupseong.
In times of war, common people moved to the sanseong for safety.
solution: 본문은 평상시 일반 백성(주로 농민)이 읍성 '성벽 밖'에 살았다고 했다. 성벽 안에 살았다는 ④는 이와 반대이므로 일치하지 않는다. 나머지 선지는 모두 본문 내용과 일치한다.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Why did the procession happen? The first thing King Jeongjo had in mind was to show respect to his family. It happened around his mother's sixtieth birthday. In the Joseon Dynasty, just like today, turning 60 had a special meaning. His father's tomb was near Hwaseong Haenggung, and he planned to hold a memorial service to honor his late father. By combining the two events, he was telling everyone how much family meant to him. But there's more. King Jeongjo was also making a statement about the Joseon Dynasty's strength. He dressed like a military leader, wearing armor and sitting on a horse with his soldiers marching in perfect order.
choices: Showing respect to his family was King Jeongjo's first purpose for the procession.
Turning 60 held a special meaning in the Joseon Dynasty.
King Jeongjo held the memorial service because his mother's tomb was near Hwaseong Haenggung.
By combining the two events, the king showed how much family meant to him.
The king wore armor to display the strength of the Joseon Dynasty.
solution: 화성 행궁 근처에 있던 것은 어머니가 아니라 '아버지'의 묘이며, 추모 행사도 돌아가신 아버지를 기리기 위한 것이었다. 따라서 어머니의 묘 때문이라고 한 ③이 일치하지 않는다. 나머지는 모두 본문에 근거한다.

King Jeongjo made sure everything was documented by creating records for the procession and the construction of Hwaseong Fortress. These construction records were especially a lifesaver when the fortress was damaged during wartime. They were also part of the reason UNESCO recognized Hwaseong as a World Heritage Site. At first, the people at UNESCO were a bit unsure about recognizing Hwaseong Fortress; they weren't totally convinced it was authentic. But after checking the translated documents and comparing them with the restored fortress, they finally agreed that the fortress had been restored just the way it was meant to be.

solution: 정조가 만든 기록(행차·축성), 기록이 유용했던 시점(전란으로 성이 손상됐을 때), 유네스코가 처음 주저한 이유(진정성에 확신이 없었음), 진정성 확인 방법(번역 문서 대조)은 모두 본문에서 답할 수 있다. 그러나 복원에 걸린 '기간(연수)'은 언급되지 않으므로 ⑤는 답할 수 없다.

Historically, the sanseong served as the final defense against invaders by utilizing Korea’s mountainous landscape to its advantage. Defenders could fight from higher ground and effectively push back enemies with fewer soldiers. A famous example of this advantage was the battle at Haengjusanseong during the Japanese invasion of Korea in the late 16th century.
Living in the sanseong was not practical due to scarce farmland and poor living conditions though. So during peaceful times, people lived in and around the eupseong, such as Naganeupseong and Haemieupseong.

Q: Why didn’t people live in the sanseong during peaceful times?
A: Because it had (1)__________ farmland and (2)__________ __________ __________.
solution: 본문의 'Living in the sanseong was not practical due to scarce farmland and poor living conditions'에서 근거를 찾는다. 평화로운 시기에 산성에 살지 않은 이유는 농지가 부족하고(scarce) 생활 여건이 열악했기(poor living conditions) 때문이다.

And here’s the cherry on top: through the procession, King Jeongjo made government more accessible. During that time, the government used to hold exams to hire officials every three years. And among the records of the procession, there are these amazing paintings. One painting, Hwaneo Haengryeoldo, doesn’t just feature the king’s crew, but it also shows ordinary people watching along the road. (A)그것은 그 당시의 일반적인 미술과는 다른 시각인데, 그 미술은 중요한 인물들에게만 초점을 맞추었다.
